primary.title: Sidereus Nuncius
primary.author: Galileo Galilei
primary.rationale: Galileo's groundbreaking report on his telescopic observations of the Moon, Jupiter's moons, and the Milky Way. It is a foundational text in the Scientific Revolution.

primary.title: Dialogo sopra i due massimi sistemi del mondo
primary.author: Galileo Galilei
primary.rationale: Galileo's most famous work, presenting arguments for the Copernican heliocentric model versus the Ptolemaic geocentric model. It led to his trial by the Inquisition.

primary.title: Discorsi e dimostrazioni matematiche intorno a due nuove scienze
primary.author: Galileo Galilei
primary.rationale: Galileo's final major work, published in Dutch exile, laying the groundwork for modern physics by discussing mechanics and the strength of materials.

secondary.title: Galileo's Daughter: A Historical Memoir of Science, Faith, and Love
secondary.author: Dava Sobel
secondary.rationale: A highly acclaimed and accessible biography that uses Galileo's daughter's letters to provide a personal and historical context for his life and work.

secondary.title: Galileo: A Very Short Introduction
secondary.author: John L. Heilbron
secondary.rationale: A concise yet authoritative overview of Galileo's life, scientific contributions, and historical significance by a leading historian of science.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Galileo
secondary.author: Nick Wilding
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Galileo's life, work, and legacy, offering in-depth scholarly analysis.

suggestions.notes: Galileo's primary works are widely available in multiple languages and editions online. The secondary sources chosen are recent, well-regarded academic books offering comprehensive overviews and detailed scholarship.
